title: JAXBench bundled optimized-reference headroom on TPU v5e

required: Identical shapes and values for XLA and Pallas arms
Device-profiled timing after compilation and warmup

summary.suite_aggregate_reason: Six of eight references are excluded, so an aggregate would misrepresent benchmark coverage.

results.reason: The optimized reference compiles under the corrected scoped-VMEM budget but fails the full-shape oracle with maximum absolute difference 0.0625.
The naive XLA baseline materializes full attention logits and uses 16.50 GiB against 15.75 GiB usable HBM. The Pallas arm runs, but no valid paired timing or independent full-shape oracle remains.
The optimized reference compiles under the corrected scoped-VMEM budget but fails the full-shape oracle with maximum absolute difference 3.4839675426483154.
The XLA input omits batch 4 while the Pallas input includes it. The optimized arm reports eight times the FLOPs, so the descriptive timings are not comparable.

The Pallas reference compiles and executes after the mechanical pltpu.ANY to pl.ANY API adapter, but its wrapper uses a different argument contract and no independent paired correctness result exists.
The Pallas reference compiles and executes after the ANY API adapter and correction of its stale 32 MiB per-kernel VMEM limit, but no independent paired correctness and timing result exists.
The unchanged reference passes correctness and normal-lowering profile proof under the corrected 64 MiB scoped-VMEM contract, but is 0.34 percent slower than XLA.
Three paired profiler repeats pass correctness after binding the baseline max_expert_size as the static value returned by create_inputs. The median paired speedup is 1.1470x.

decision.interpretation: The calibrated benchmark demonstrates one fusion-rich Pallas headroom case and one optimized GEMM at XLA parity. It does not support an eight-workload aggregate performance claim.
